rows.name: ? block 2x2 tile-id table entry [TL,BL,TR,BR] (World 1-1 ? block source)
rows.notes: Origin of the World 1-1 ? block's four 8x8 tile ids. A run of those nametable ids lives in a table of 4-byte metatile entries [top-left, bottom-left, top-right, bottom-right] at prgRom offset 0x8C8C (CPU $8C8C): 53 55 54 56. An identical duplicate entry sits at 0x8C90 (a second ? block type). The renderer at CPU $88E7-$8906 reads it: LDA $06A1,X (block type) / ASL A / ASL A / ADC (($071F&1)<<1) / TAY ; LDX $00 ; LDA ($06),Y / STA $0344,X ; INY / LDA ($06),Y / STA $0345,X - it copies one 2-byte column (TL,BL or TR,BR) into the VRAM buffer. Proof (search and ledgered write): search_memory prgRom '53 55 54 56' returned 0xC8C and 0xC90 (row-major '53 54 55 56' matched nothing); write_memory prgRom 0x8C8C 0x53 -> 0x24 (blank sky), reset_emulator, pressed Start twice and walked right - the ? block's top-left 8x8 vanished: nametable 1 addr 0x2640 held 0x24 while 0x2641/0x2660/0x2661 stayed 0x54/0x55/0x56, and get_pixel_color on the missing quadrant read periwinkle $22; undo_edit restored 0x53.

rows.name: small Mario standing-frame tile ids (prgRom 0x6ECF pose entry)
rows.notes: Origin of small Mario's standing-frame tile ids. The player sprite handler reads an 8-byte-per-pose table (rows top->bottom, two tiles per row); the standing pose entry at prgRom offset 0x6ECF (CPU $EECF) is FC FC FC FC 3A 37 4F 4F - the top two rows are the blank padding tile 0xFC (the player is drawn in the big-Mario 2x4 layout even when small), and the visible 2x2 is 0x3A (top-left) 0x37 (top-right) 0x4F (bottom-left) 0x4F (bottom-right, drawn h-flipped). Proof (search and ledgered write): search_memory prgRom '3A 37 4F 4F' returned only 0x6ED3, the head-left byte inside this pose entry; write_memory prgRom 0x6ED3 0x3A -> 0x4F, reset_emulator, pressed Start twice - at the 1-1 start list_sprites showed the OAM entry at (40,193) with chr_tile 0x4F instead of 0x3A (the standing frame's head-left tile), and the screenshot showed Mario's upper-left sprite changed; undo_edit restored 0x3A and the next start read 0x3A again. Neighbouring entries are other poses (e.g. 0x6EBF = FC FC FC FC 3A 37 92 93); the table runs from ~0x6E40 and ends at 0x6EE8, with code (LDA absolute) starting at 0x6EE9.
